pages.text: "My turn to throw, Grandpa!" Bung gripped a small net. Their boat floated tied still. Grandpa's freshly thrown net lay round and wide on the water.
"I want mine to open like yours." Grandpa stood behind and held Bung's waist. "Go on."
"Heeyah!" Bung threw. The net flew in a fist-sized bunch. The earlier try had dropped just like that. "Why will it not open?"
Bung dropped the net on the floor and sat. "I cannot. Bunched twice!" Ddori fiddled with the wet net.
Grandpa lifted it and draped half on Bung's arm. "Grip it all, and it bunches. Half on your arm, half in your hand." He showed a slow body turn.
Bung gripped half, turned once, and threw. It landed half open. "Wider than before!" Grandpa nodded. "Bunched net? Try again!"
The fourth throw bunched again. Still, Bung shook the net out and stood. "All right. Bunched net? Try again!" Ddori stamped, ankle bell jingling.
Fifth throw—wide open! A circle on the water. Bung drew Ddori's hand close to show it. "That is my throw!"
Grandpa pulled it in. A little fish flapped. "One, grip only half! Two, turn once! Three, if it fails, throw again!" Bung wiped wet hands on the trousers.
Grandpa hugged Bung and patted a shoulder. "A little wider with each throw." "Tomorrow morning too! Bunched net? Try again!" Bung draped it over an arm.
